title: The £30 Demob Gratuity Jack Cohen Spent on a Hackney Barrow
conflicts: Age in 1919 given as 21 (Jewish Chronicle, Irish Examiner, Hackney Council) or 20 (Hackney Gazette): story gives only his birth year. First shops dated 1929, 1931 or 1932 across accounts: story says early 1930s. First-day figure (£1 profit, with £4 sales in some retellings) is available only from the Irish Examiner among loadable sources: story gives the £1 and attributes it.
notes: Hesiod's 'add a little to a little' line was the first choice but is already used. Osmanieh rescue and cap-throwing rest on the Jewish Chronicle's 2019 profile and are attributed. The Grocer's promotional feature (archived copy) agrees on £1 profit from £4 sales but is paid content and was not cited; Tesco's own history page renders by script and was not used.
